semanticReviewCriteria: pMapIterable accepts an optional `signal` alongside concurrency/backpressure; when already aborted, the first consumer next() rejects with the exact signal.reason before any source iterator.next() or mapper invocation.

On mid-iteration abort the pending consumer next() rejects promptly with the identical reason object, no further source next() calls are issued, no new mapper calls start, and no mapper result is yielded after the abort is observed even if running mappers settle later.

The source iterator's return() is called best-effort on abort when the method exists (errors swallowed), and the abort listener is removed on normal completion, source failure, mapper failure, abort, and early consumer exit (generator return/throw).
The no-signal code path is behaviorally identical to baseline: ordering, concurrency capping, backpressure capping, pMapSkip handling, and error propagation are unchanged.
The exported pMap function and its existing abort contract are untouched, and no new module-level dependencies or imports are added.

Every new AVA test is deterministic: deferred promises and counters only, no wall-clock sleeps or timing ranges; the six required scenarios are all covered including abort-with-never-fired completion.

advisoryNotes.text: TASK.md states the runtime implementation and its behavioral regression tests must pass together and neither is an acceptable partial result, so they share one repair authority: a failing behavioral test may require repairing index.js.
Do not modify pMap or any code path it shares; implement abort state inside pMapIterable's generator only. The existing pMap signal listener pattern is precedent to mirror, not to refactor.

An abort may fire while a spawned promise awaits iterator.next() or while the consumer loop awaits promises[0]; the consumer-facing rejection must not depend on long-running mappers or a hung source, e.g. race the consumer await against an abort-aware rejection. Implementation shape is the worker's choice within the stated semantics.

Use hand-rolled deferred promises and invocation counters for the new tests; the `delay`/`timeSpan` usages already present in test.js are legacy baseline and must remain, but no new sleep may be introduced.
